cands.name: Victor Arias
cands.bio: Democratic nominee. Cape Coral attorney (owner of Arias Law Firm since 2003), born in the Dominican Republic and raised in New York. Moved to Southwest Florida in 1999 to work for the School District of Lee County, where he later served as an attorney. Has not held elective office.
cands.local_ties: Cape Coral; in Southwest Florida since 1999.

record.text: Practice areas reported as personal injury, workers' compensation and school law; won the Aug 2026 primary with 45% (15,406 votes) over Howard Sapp and Robert Neeld.
Stated priorities: the economy ('too much suffering'), water quality and the environment, more money in workers' pockets, lower grocery and gas prices.

cands.gaps: No photo found. The only campaign site found is a pages.dev address that a September roundup described as suspended and that returned an error when I opened it; treat with caution. Social accounts and endorsements not found. Note: victorarias.com is an unrelated Primerica agent, not the candidate.

cands.name: Jim Schwartzel
cands.bio: Republican nominee. President of Fort Myers-based Sun Broadcasting (radio and TV stations; also owns Gulfshore Life and Gulfshore Business magazines). Has never held elective office. Won a 10-candidate primary with about 29%, ahead of Trump-endorsed Catalina Lauf. Seat is open (Byron Donalds ran for governor).
cands.local_ties: Grew up in Fort Myers, Bishop Verot High School, Stetson University 1998; took over the family broadcasting company in 2012. New District 19 drops Fort Myers and extends west in Lee County into inland Collier County.

record.text: Led opposition to Republican-backed 2023 and 2024 Florida bills that would have made it easier to sue media outlets (both failed); received the 2023 Pete Weitzel Friend of the First Amendment Award.
Business Observer noted open questions about whether his ownership of local media could influence coverage if elected; he said FCC rules and editorial independence would be followed.

Stated priorities: SAVE America Act, continued deportations, septic-to-sewer conversion, and a proposed SR 29/Immokalee to SR 82 bypass; says development is vital to jobs with zoning left to counties.

money_notes.text: Put $1 million of his own money into the campaign (as of Nov 2025).
Said he beat opponents who raised '$15 million' (his claim; not verified by the reporter).

endorsements.text: Post-primary: Donald Trump and Gov. Ron DeSantis (as listed on Wikipedia). During the primary: House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Rep. Jim Jordan, former Sen. Connie Mack III and former Rep. Connie Mack IV. Trump had endorsed primary rival Catalina Lauf on Aug 13.

cands.gaps: No photo found. Social handles not verified. Outside spending in the general not found.

cands.name: Seth Haskin
cands.bio: No-party-affiliation candidate, 26, who manages his family's coffee shop business. Bachelor's degree in neuroscience. Describes himself as a 'strict constitutionalist'; previously ran for governor of Wisconsin as a write-in. Has not held office.
cands.local_ties: Described by NPR as an independent candidate from Naples, Fla.

record.text: Platform: restore Congress's role over war powers, simplify federal regulation, expand the House by 100-200 members, repeal the 16th Amendment, move toward a metal-backed dollar, balanced budgets (campaign profile on BallotReady).
Told NPR he is running as an independent because he believes both parties are influenced by industry leaders, PAC money and foreign lobbies, and hopes for a double-digit share.

cands.gaps: No photo found. Ballot name is 'Seth Haskin' (Wikipedia spells it Haskins). Social handles taken from BallotReady listing, not opened directly.
